Hot Path Lab

The Reef's sonar asks "have I reported this fish before?" for every visible fish, every frame. Make each question cheaper, or change how many questions it takes. Watch which one bends the curve.

The Reef's sonar, mid-range phone, 30 fps. Goal: Sonar.Update at most 1 ms, at minute 10 of a dive with 3,000 fish visible (the festival).

Lesson 036: algorithms before micro-optimizations

    
    
    
    Lesson 044 · Challenge: predict first, then tap Set up and check
    
    
      
  
      

  
      
    
      What this shows
      
    
      
      
      Count the work first
      Visible fish × half the list is over a million compares a frame. No compare is cheap enough to make a million of them fit in 1 ms.
      
      
      Tuning buys a constant
      A week of tuning made each compare 2.7× cheaper. The line is lower, but it still climbs with the list, and the festival puts it back over budget.
      
      
      An algorithm buys the curve
      A hash set answers "seen before?" in about the same time however many fish it holds. The line goes flat. It costs about 5× the memory.
      
    
      
    
      This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 036's numbers: the reported list grows by 300 fish a minute; a found fish is, on average, halfway down the list; one compare costs 8 ns through object.Equals (a struct without IEquatable, boxed) or 3 ns after the tuning week; a HashSet lookup costs 25 ns. Memory: 4 bytes per id in the list, about 20 bytes per id in the set. New fish per frame are few and are left out.
